math-bit-manipulation__sqrt-x.title: Sqrt(x)
math-bit-manipulation__sqrt-x.pattern: Binary search on the answer (integer square root)
math-bit-manipulation__sqrt-x.statement: Given a non-negative integer `x`, return the integer square root of `x`, i.e. `floor(sqrt(x))`. The decimal part is truncated and you must not use any built-in exponent/sqrt function.

approaches.name: Binary search on the root
approaches.idea: Search `mid` in `[1, x/2]` for the largest value whose square does not exceed `x`. `mid*mid` is monotonic, so a value works iff every smaller value works — a classic monotone predicate. Use `long` for the square to avoid `int` overflow when `mid*mid` exceeds `2^31-1`. When the loop ends, `hi` holds `floor(sqrt(x))`.

math-bit-manipulation__sqrt-x.insight: Monotone predicate `mid*mid <= x` -> binary search; use `long` for the square to dodge overflow, and the answer is `hi` after the loop.

math-bit-manipulation__excel-column.title: Excel Column
math-bit-manipulation__excel-column.statement: Excel labels columns `A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ...`. Two conversions are needed: (1) given a column title string, return its 1-based column number; (2) given a column number, return its title. The catch is that this is a **bijective** base-26 system: digits run `1..26` (A..Z) with no zero, so the reverse conversion needs a `--` decrement each step.
constraints: columnTitle consists of uppercase English letters

approaches.name: Title -> number (Horner in base 26)
approaches.idea: Treat the string as a base-26 number where `A=1..Z=26`. Sweep left to right accumulating `result = result*26 + (c - 'A' + 1)`, exactly like reading a decimal number digit by digit (Horner's rule).

approaches.name: Number -> title (bijective base-26)
approaches.idea: Because there is no digit 0, subtract 1 before each `% 26` so the remainder maps to `A..Z` (0..25). Emit the least significant letter, divide by 26, repeat, then reverse. The `columnNumber--` is what converts ordinary base-26 into the offset (bijective) system.

math-bit-manipulation__excel-column.insight: It is base-26 with no zero: decoding is plain Horner, but encoding needs a `--` before each `%26`/`/26` step.

math-bit-manipulation__count-primes.title: Count Primes
math-bit-manipulation__count-primes.statement: Given an integer `n`, return the number of prime numbers strictly less than `n`.

approaches.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
approaches.idea: Mark composites: for each prime `i`, cross out its multiples. Start crossing from `i*i` (smaller multiples were already marked by smaller primes) and only iterate `i` up to `sqrt(n)` implicitly by testing `!composite[i]`. Count the entries never marked. Use a `long` for `i*i` to avoid overflow near the upper bound.

math-bit-manipulation__count-primes.insight: Sieve, and start marking multiples at `i*i` (not `2*i`) — everything below is already handled.

math-bit-manipulation__fraction-to-recur.title: Fraction to Recurring Decimal
math-bit-manipulation__fraction-to-recur.pattern: Long division + remainder memoization to detect the cycle
math-bit-manipulation__fraction-to-recur.statement: Given `numerator` and `denominator` of a fraction, return the fraction as a string. If the fractional part is repeating, wrap the repeating block in parentheses. Handle the sign and integer overflow (`INT_MIN` numerator/denominator).

approaches.name: Simulate long division, memoize remainders
approaches.idea: Emit the integer part, then perform long division on the fractional part. A repeating decimal appears exactly when a remainder repeats, so store each remainder's output position in a map; when a remainder recurs, insert `(` at its stored position and append `)`. Cast to `long` and take absolute values first so the sign logic (XOR of the two signs) and `INT_MIN` are handled without overflow.
approaches.time: O(d) where d is the number of distinct remainders (< |denominator|)

math-bit-manipulation__fraction-to-recur.insight: A repeating fraction == a repeating remainder; map remainder -> position and wrap in parentheses when it recurs. Do arithmetic in `long` after `abs` to survive `INT_MIN`.

math-bit-manipulation__basic-calculator-.title: Basic Calculator I/II/III
math-bit-manipulation__basic-calculator-.pattern: Stack for precedence + recursion for parentheses
math-bit-manipulation__basic-calculator-.statement: Implement a calculator that evaluates a string expression. The general form (Calculator III) supports non-negative integers and the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` with normal precedence and arbitrary parentheses; division truncates toward zero. Calculator I is the special case with only `+`, `-`, and parentheses; Calculator II has `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` but no parentheses. The single solution below handles all three.
constraints: s consists of digits, '+', '-', '*', '/', '(', ')', and spaces
s is a valid expression; integer values fit in a signed 32-bit range

approaches.name: Recursive descent on '(' with an operator/operand stack
approaches.idea: Scan left to right building the current number. On seeing `(`, recurse to evaluate the sub-expression and use its value as the current number. When the next token is an operator (or the string/parenthesis ends), flush the pending number using the *previous* operator: push for `+`, push negated for `-`, and for `*`/`/` pop the top and combine — this defers low-precedence ops on the stack while resolving high-precedence ones immediately. The answer is the sum of the stack. A shared index (`int[] i`) lets the recursion consume characters across calls.

math-bit-manipulation__basic-calculator-.insight: Push +/- terms onto a stack but resolve */ immediately against the top; recurse on `(` sharing one index. Final answer = sum of the stack.

math-bit-manipulation__max-points-on-a-l.title: Max Points on a Line
math-bit-manipulation__max-points-on-a-l.pattern: Fix a point, group the rest by normalized slope (gcd)
math-bit-manipulation__max-points-on-a-l.statement: Given `n` distinct points on the 2D plane, return the maximum number of points that lie on the same straight line.

approaches.name: Anchor point + slope counting with reduced fractions
approaches.idea: For each anchor `i`, every other point defines a slope `(dy, dx)`. Points share a line through `i` iff they share the same slope, so count slopes in a map and take the max. To use an exact (float-free) key, reduce `(dy, dx)` by their gcd and normalize the sign (make `dx > 0`, or `dx == 0 => dy > 0`) so `(1,2)` and `(-1,-2)` collapse to one key. Answer for the anchor is `bestSlopeCount + 1` (the anchor itself).

math-bit-manipulation__max-points-on-a-l.insight: Fix each point and bucket the others by gcd-reduced, sign-normalized slope; the biggest bucket + 1 is the line through that anchor.

math-bit-manipulation__super-pow.title: Super Pow
math-bit-manipulation__super-pow.pattern: Modular exponentiation, digit by digit (Horner mod)
math-bit-manipulation__super-pow.statement: Compute `a^b mod 1337`, where `a` is a positive integer and `b` is an extremely large positive integer given as an array of its decimal digits (most significant first).
constraints: b has no leading zeros except the number 0 itself

approaches.name: Horner over digits with modular power
approaches.idea: Use `a^(10*prefix + d) = (a^prefix)^10 * a^d`. Fold the digits left to right (Horner's rule) keeping the running result mod 1337: at each digit set `result = powMod(result, 10) * powMod(a, d)`. Since exponents are single digits, `powMod` just multiplies at most 10 times, all under the modulus, so no big-integer arithmetic is needed.
approaches.time: O(L) with a small constant (<= 10 mults per digit)

math-bit-manipulation__super-pow.insight: a^(10k+d) = (a^k)^10 * a^d — Horner-fold the digit array while reducing mod 1337 each step.

math-bit-manipulation__nth-magical-numbe.title: Nth Magical Number
math-bit-manipulation__nth-magical-numbe.pattern: Binary search on the answer + inclusion-exclusion count via LCM
math-bit-manipulation__nth-magical-numbe.statement: A positive integer is *magical* if it is divisible by `a` or by `b`. Return the `n`-th magical number, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

approaches.name: Binary search on value, count multiples with LCM
approaches.idea: The count of magical numbers `<= x` is `x/a + x/b - x/lcm(a,b)` by inclusion-exclusion, and this count is non-decreasing in `x` — a monotone predicate. Binary search the smallest `x` whose count reaches `n`. Bound the high end by `min(a,b) * n` (at most that many are needed) and use `long` throughout to avoid overflow; take the result mod 1e9+7 only at the very end.

math-bit-manipulation__nth-magical-numbe.insight: Count(<= x) = x/a + x/b - x/lcm is monotone -> binary search the answer; reduce mod only at the end.
